entries.reason: the expansion of a 5/6/5 word to 8/8/8, which Conversion.h writes out
entries.effect: red and blue (5 * 255 + 15) / 31 and green (6 * 255 + 31) / 63, in that order; the refusals are the release's own as below
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4, which writes the per-channel arithmetic out; the host's own vImage, compared byte for byte in tests/backports/host/vimagepixels, over the corners of each word; the release's own armv7 caches, which say which release first exports the name

entries.reason: Conversion.h gives no formula for this one, only that a caller who wants the alpha handled should convert to eight bits first, so the port does exactly that: the 1/5/5/5 word up to 8/8/8/8 and the 5/6/5 word down from it, which is the header's own 'first at high bitdepth, then convert to lower bitdepth'
entries.effect: the 1/5/5/5 word expanded and narrowed, and not a bit shift: red and blue (5 * 255 + 15) / 31 then (8 * 31 + 127) / 255 and green (5 * 255 + 15) / 31 then (8 * 63 + 127) / 255, packed as (red << 11) | (green << 5) | blue; the refusals are the release's own as below
entries.source: the header of iOS 16.4, which writes the per-channel arithmetic out; the host's own vImage, compared byte for byte in tests/backports/host/vimagepixels, over the corners of each word; the release's own armv7 caches, which say which release first exports the name
